items.title: Mapping Road Safety Inequity in India Using Artificial Intelligence Where Fatalities Cluster, Where AI Road-Safety Technology Is Deployed, and What Should Be Prioritised
items.abstract: India records more road deaths than any other country in the world, with 172,890 in 2023, but the public data behind that number is rarely studied to ask whether the danger is spread evenly and whether new artificial-intelligence road-safety technology is reaching the worst impacted areas. This paper uses official Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) figures for the country, for every state and union territory, and for fifty cities, together with a list of few of India’s AI road-safety deployments, to map where road deaths cluster and to compare that with where the technology has already been installed. Then, it builds a simple, literature-based model of how many lives the proven tools could theoretically save. The work is quantitative, with fifteen figures and six tables. The main results are as follows. The absolute and per-person data are almost unrelated, with a correlation of only 0.28, so Uttar Pradesh has the most deaths but only an average rate per person, while Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, and Telangana have the highest rates per person. AI systems have mostly been implemented in states that already had strong administration rather than to the worst impacted ones, which matches the World Bank’s split between high-capacity and low-capacity states. A preventable-fraction model estimates that AI-suited vehicle and enforcement measures could prevent roughly 26,000 deaths a year at moderate coverage, in a range of 11,900 to 49,500, with automated speed enforcement the largest single measure at 17,600. Even the high estimate is below the national target of halving deaths by 2030, so road engineering and emergency care must take over the burden of covering the rest. Most of the preventable deaths fall in the worst impacted states that currently have no major deployment, which shows the real cost of the deployment gap.

items.title: Maritime transport and policy research over the past 50 years: a review across four maritime journals
items.abstract: Journal focused bibliometric studies, especially those examining leading or highly relevant journals, are widely acknowledged as an effective way to capture the intellectual structure of a field. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of four important journals which have strong orientation in maritime transport and policy field using R-Bibliometrix package and VOSviewer. The final dataset consists of 2,889 articles published between 1976 and 2024. The results mapped the intellectual research landscape of the field by identifying leading authors, institutions, regions, influential articles, and major research clusters. Keyword co-occurrence analysis shows that the most frequently discussed topics include ports operations, logistics, container shipping, maritime safety, and climate change adaptation. The field also engages with promising areas of human-centred issues such as seafarer, maritime education and training, human factors, human error and non-technical skills. The findings show an interesting direction that integrates economic and technical operations with human and societal dimensions. Additionally, the findings potentially provide insights for researchers and practitioners seeking collaborations or directions, and policymakers seeking priorities in the maritime transport and policy domain.

items.title: Market Incentives for AI Safety Investment
items.abstract: Despite their practical significance, modern AI systems pose significant societal risks, including toxicity, malicious use, and misinformation. Their mitigation depends not only on technical feasibility but also on the incentives of firms that develop and deploy these systems. We show how profit maximization shapes safety investment in an AI supply chain with an upstream LLM provider and several competing downstream firms. In our game-theoretic model, we derive the market-driven level of safety investment and compare it with the levels that maximize market welfare and industry profit. We find that downstream competition generally induces downstream firms to invest more in safety than the industry-profit-optimal level. By contrast, the upstream provider may underinvest relative to these benchmarks because it is not fully compensated for the surplus from safety investments. Finally, we analyze how different regulatory interventions affect the participants' incentives and profits, and the resulting levels of model safety.

items.abstract: Abstract We shine a spotlight on marketing misinformation—claims about products and brands that contradict or distort verifiable facts. Misinformation may be created unintentionally or intentionally by companies, competitors, customers, or third parties seeking to harm companies or consumers. We focus on the role of AI in creating, obfuscating, and disseminating misinformation in the form of text, audio, images, and videos generated using large language models. This type of information can pose a substantial risk for brand safety. Consumers may be aware that AI can generate misinformation but may lack the ability to guard against it. We discuss how different stakeholders in the information ecosystem can help in the prevention and correction of misinformation and propose a future research agenda in this critical and fast‐growing area.

items.title: Materials foundation models fail together: Correlated errors and collective blind spots
items.abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) are increasingly combined to screen candidate crystals, but the reliability gains from consensus and disagreement depend on diversity among model errors. We quantify error dependence across 15 public uMLIPs using density functional theory (DFT) convex-hull distances for 248,623 structures from the Wang–Botti–Marques benchmark. The mean pairwise error correlation is 0.39, corresponding to 4.3 effective models. Because rank-1 removal cannot distinguish shared model bias from shared reference effects, we applied two additive-reference controls; correlations remained 0.44 and 0.42, with effective model counts of 3.7 and 3.9. A stratified permutation null that preserves each model’s coupling to the DFT reference while destroying cross-model correlation showed that false discoveries shared by single-model, consensus, and agreement-based screening occurred 141 times more often than expected ( p < 0.001 ). Agreement-gated screening admitted 1620 false discoveries versus 7 under the null. The median consensus did not outperform the best individual model and produced a 27.6% false-discovery rate among predicted-stable structures. Cross-model disagreement was nearly uninformative (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC, 0.51), whereas the consensus margin reached AUC 0.75 and conformal-normalized margin 0.85; standard split-conformal intervals reached 0.68. Removing the 30% of candidates closest to the threshold reduced the retained false-discovery rate to 17.8%, but was exactly equivalent to tightening the stability threshold at matched shortlist size. These results show that correlated errors can limit ensemble reliability and that threshold-aware scores provide a practical ranking of screening risk. We release a reproducible reliability atlas and benchmark.

items.title: Measuring a scaffold from inside: an operator-authored self-measurement harness for a constitutional runtime over a hosted language model
items.abstract: Interactive intelligent systems constructed over hosted large language models cannot retrain the substrate on which they depend, and so their designers enforce a named epistemology at the surrounding scaffold layer. A difficulty follows that has received little methodological attention: when quality regresses, the regression frequently belongs to the scaffold rather than the substrate, and identifying it requires instruments that measure the scaffold itself rather than the model beneath it. This article reports one such instrument set, added to a live constitutional runtime between 17 and 18 July 2026 and extended with a production drift observer on 19 August 2026, and situates it as a reusable design pattern. The layer comprises six components—operator-authored adversarial batteries held as versioned regression fixtures, deterministic pattern screens encoding named defects, an emission quarantine that retains failure evidence as a first-class object, an instrument-health monitor issuing autonomous handoffs, continuous-integration delivery tripwires, and an observe-only production drift detector that accumulates a hand-labelling corpus from live traffic without altering any replies. Eight falsifiable harness predictions are stated (H1 through H8), each named against a specific runtime carrier—a code path, a database table, or a typed field—and each paired with an explicit falsification condition; their relationship to the eight pre-registered outcome predictions (F1 through F8) of a companion architecture paper is stated in a dedicated reconciliation section, since the harness reported here is the instrument set on which those outcome predictions depend. Of the eight, five (H1, H2, H3, H5, H7) carry dated on-platform observations and are reported in a dedicated observed subsection; three (H4, H6, H8) are prospective—predictions about experiments that have not yet occurred—and are reported separately under that label, so that no reader mistakes the distribution of evidence. The predictions are offered for adversarial replication under an honest empirical frame rather than as settled results: the batteries were authored by the platform’s operator, classification is not independent, and the number of platforms studied is one. The discussion states a narrow priority claim, distinguishes the enforcement point of composition-time assertion from adjacent techniques, extends the pattern to the governance of learning loops—a scaffold that adapts must be measured by the same discipline that measures a scaffold that enforces—and argues that the interaction properties a reader encounters, an observation lock and per-turn provenance grounding, become testable precisely because they are structurally enforced.

items.title: Measuring Creativity as a Gateway to Innovation
items.abstract: Measuring creativity has always felt like wandering down a cul-de-sac: Everyone agrees it’s important, yet their attempts to pin it down often lead nowhere. Traditional tests - like counting how many new uses someone can dream up for a paper clip - capture flashes of cleverness but say little about whether those ideas would actually work in the messy real world. Over the decades, researchers from Terman to Torrance to Martinsen have wrestled with the problem, but measurements of creativity have had a way of slipping through their fingers. The OECD’s PISA 2022 framework tried to shrug off some of these limitations by adding new dimensions such as written expression, visual expression, and scientific problem-solving. The first wave of results in 2023 not only looked promising but also revealed fresh complications: Students could generate copious ideas, but scoring them fairly remained a challenge. Some responses were brilliant, and others seemed like abject failures, but even the failures sometimes contained a spark of originality that defied conventional rubrics. Now, with generative AI reshaping how we think, learn, and create, the task is shifting again. Future assessments like PISA 2029’s Media & AI Literacy module may finally begin to capture aspects of creativity once overlooked, from digital storytelling to collaborative problem-solving in human-machine teams. The broader lesson is clear: Measuring creativity is not about designing one flawless test but about accepting human frailties, staying flexible, and continuously adapting our definitions and evaluations of imagination as new tools and contexts emerge.

items.title: Measuring Successful Cooperation in Human-AI Teamwork: Development and Validation of the Perceived Cooperativity and Teaming Perception Scales
items.abstract: As human–AI cooperation becomes increasingly prevalent, reliable instruments for assessing the subjective quality of cooperative human–AI interaction are needed. We introduce two theoretically grounded scales: the Perceived Cooperativity Scale (PCS), grounded in joint activity theory, and the Teaming Perception Scale (TPS), grounded in evolutionary cooperation theory. The PCS captures an agent’s perceived cooperative capability and practice within a single interaction sequence; the TPS captures the emergent sense of teaming arising from mutual contribution and support. Both scales were adapted for human–human cooperation to enable cross-agent comparisons. Across three studies (complete N=409) encompassing a cooperative card game (N1=94), LLM interaction (N2=182), and a decision-support system (N3=133), analyses of dimensionality, reliability, and validity indicated that both scales successfully differentiated between cooperation partners of varying cooperative quality and showed construct validity in line with expectations. The scales provide a basis for empirical investigation and system evaluation across a wide range of human–AI cooperation contexts.

items.title: MechaScreener: Large language model-based automated screening for systematic reviews and research
items.abstract: Systematic reviews are the gold standard for evidence synthesis, but the manual title and abstract screening of thousands of references creates a severe bottleneck. Existing automated tools have historically struggled to achieve the near-perfect recall (sensitivity) required for reliable reviews. We developed MechaScreener as a 'zero-shot' automated screening tool that utilises a large language model to rank article relevance. The tool requires no initial training data or manual pre-screening, as MechaScreener directly applies user-provided question elements (PICO) or inclusion/exclusion criteria to assign an ordinal relevance score (1-5) to each reference. We evaluated the tool in two phases: a development phase using five reference libraries to optimise prompts, and an independent evaluation phase using 10 diverse Cochrane review libraries (comprising both randomised controlled trials [RCTs] and non-RCTs) containing over 58,000 references. In the evaluation dataset, MechaScreener achieved a perfect recall of 1.00 (100%) in all 10 reviews, ensuring that no relevant articles were missed (pooled record-level 95% CI: 0.98-1.00). Concurrently, it achieved an overall macro-average specificity of 0.61 (61%, cluster bootstrap 95% CI: 0.46-0.75; pooled record-level specificity 0.59, 95% CI: 0.59-0.60). Specificity varied from 0.21 in broad public health topics to 0.91 in precise pharmacological interventions, reflecting the tool's built-in conservatism when evaluating ambiguous abstracts. By safely eliminating over 60% of irrelevant literature during the initial screening phase without compromising recall, MechaScreener functions as a highly reliable but low-effort 'first-pass' filter, allowing researchers to substantially reduce manual workloads and reallocate resources towards full-text review and data extraction.

items.title: MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Agent memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to reuse past experiences without updating their parameters. However, semantic similarity alone does not guarantee memory usefulness: downstream performance depends on how memories are selected and presented to the agent. We propose MemComposer, a memory composer that jointly examines the current query and retrieved candidates to decide which experiences to include, how many to select, and how to order them. We train the composer using Experience Policy Optimization (ExPO), a GRPO-based framework that evaluates assembled memory contexts through complete agent interactions and uses task-success feedback to optimize the assembly policy. Across three $τ^2$-bench domains with two frozen executors, MemComposer outperforms the strongest baseline for each executor while reducing average memory-token usage by 16.9% and 4.9%, respectively. The learned policy also transfers to unseen domains, executors, and memory banks, and benefits from memories generated by stronger models without further training. These results demonstrate the value of learning query-specific memory assembly using downstream task feedback.

items.title: MemCut: Every Secret Leaves a Trail in the Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents
items.abstract: Long-term memory has become a crucial component of large language model (LLM) agents, with most research focusing on retrieving relevant information accurately and efficiently. However, a dependable memory system must also forget sensitive user data upon request. To evaluate this capability, we introduce MemCut, a systematic benchmark for user-requested forgetting. Its 456 hand-designed secrets in long-horizon conversations have fully annotated evidence trails to test recovery after deletion, including from messages that never state the secrets directly. We propose two recovery metrics. Native recovery measures reader success through the system's retrieval, whereas residual recovery measures the same reader's success when directly given surviving objects traced to annotated disclosures or evidence. We establish three reference deletion baselines to test how far existing retrievers and write models support forgetting across five memory designs and four LLMs. Disclosure removal reduces native recovery far more than residual recovery. LLM-guided deletion of ten additional turns from twenty retrieval candidates leaves 39-76% residual recovery. Subset sweeps (144 facts, three systems, two models) show that widening the pool at a fixed budget reduces residual recovery more than deleting all original candidates. These sweeps identify candidate coverage as a bottleneck in the reference baselines.

items.title: Memorilla: Latent Semantic Memory for LLMs
items.abstract: Memory enables large language models (LLMs) to use information beyond their parameters, such as past user conversations, long documents, or an agent's earlier actions. For a frozen LLM, access to this accumulated knowledge is limited to what a memory system places in its context window. However, gathering and combining relevant information needed for each query while keeping the model's context short remains challenging for existing systems. Here we introduce Memorilla, a memory system that gathers information from an entire document collection into a fixed number of query-dependent 'memory tokens' for a frozen LLM. Memorilla encodes documents (such as user chats, book chapters) once into reusable embeddings, then learns to retrieve and place query-specific information in the LLM's input embedding space. Using only 16 memory tokens, Memorilla achieves the best performance against baselines including Mem0 and MemoRAG on five of eight benchmarks spanning personalization, long-document and knowledge-intensive question answering. Notably, on FactKG, it reaches 84.33% accuracy versus 80.43% with full-context inference, while using 108x fewer tokens to represent the source documents. Furthermore, Memorilla can facilitate continual learning in agentic systems where the document count (the agent's past turns) increases throughout the trajectory. In a TextWorld environment, we show that Memorilla reduces the agent's tendency to wander between rooms it has already explored, and improves its average success rate from 18.6% with full-history in-context learning to 24.2%. Overall, Memorilla aids frozen LLMs in accumulating and using knowledge effectively across long-context interactions and takes a step towards building continually learning AI systems.

items.title: Metaheuristic optimized and explainable machine learning for predicting the compressive strength of lightweight foamed concrete
items.abstract: Abstract Lightweight foamed concrete (LFC) can provide reduced structural dead load and enhanced thermal performance, however the compressive strength of LFC is determined by the complex nonlinear interactions between the mixture constituents, density and testing age, which makes the prediction and proportioning of the product difficult. This study addresses this challenge through leakage-resistant machine learning combined with metaheuristic optimization and explainable artificial intelligence. A literature-derived database of 993 observations was divided by mix-design group into 795 development records representing 276 groups and 198 unseen-test records representing 69 independent groups, with no overlap. Random forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) models, together with their Leopard Seal Optimizer (LSO), Harris Hawks Optimizer (HHO), and Slime Mould Algorithm (SMA) optimized variants, were assessed using 10-fold grouped cross-validation and a completely held-out test set. SHAP and PDP-ICE analyses were subsequently applied to the best-generalizing model. LSO-XGB achieved the strongest grouped out-of-fold performance ((R 2 = 0.888); RMSE = 3.93 MPa), whereas HHO-XGB performed best on unseen data ((R 2 = 0.875); RMSE = 4.10 MPa), reducing the baseline-XGB RMSE by 4.1%. HHO-XGB also produced a median absolute error of 0.82 MPa, with 95.96% and 97.47% of predictions within 5 and 10 MPa, respectively. Binder was the dominant predictor, contributing 45.4% of the global SHAP importance, followed by measured density at 16.9%. The proposed framework within the represented data domain can support preliminary LFC mixture screening and guide locally validated, multi-objective experimental designs balancing strength, density, cost, and environmental impact.

Methods Following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and PubMed Central from inception to July 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and backward citation searching. Human primary studies were screened and charted; findings were synthesized narratively. Results Of 58 identified records, 49 remained after deduplication, 35 full texts were assessed, and 28 studies were included. The evidence was predominantly observational. Taxonomic findings varied across populations, while studies of microbial functions, metabolites, multi-omics signatures, and treatment response suggested potential for biological stratification. Microbiome-targeted interventions and artificial intelligence models remain exploratory. Discussion Microbiome-derived biomarkers and predictive models require standardized methods, independent validation, and prospective evidence of clinical utility before routine psychiatric use.

items.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

items.title: Model-as-a-Trojan: Self-Activating Covert DNS Exfiltration Baked Into the Weights of an LLM Agent
items.abstract: Open-weight models are downloaded from public hubs and run inside agent harnesses that grant them tools, most powerfully, a shell, under the assumption that a sandbox contains whatever the model might do. This paper demonstrates that the assumption has a blind spot: the weights themselves can be the malware, and the sandbox's last open door, DNS, is enough. We fine-tune an open-weight LLM so that a single covert behavior lives in its parameters: on the first turn of every conversation, whenever the model infers from its context that a shell tool is available, it emits one self-contained command that reads a secret from the runtime environment, base32-encodes it, chunks it, and exfiltrates it as DNS queries toward an attacker-controlled authoritative name server. It then answers the user normally and never mentions, or repeats, the act. Because the channel is DNS, the attack completes from inside a container with no internet egress beyond name resolution - measured payload-level and model-level behind an egress firewall that drops every non-DNS packet, with the secret reconstructed from the gateway resolver's query log. Because the behavior lives in the weights, prompting is the only off-switch a victim has, and it is unreliable: the implant fires in 20/20 of adversarial suppression trials, deflects direct interrogation without disclosing the sequence, and sweeps a 45-cell sandbox-fault matrix across five tool-calling formats - plus a fresh post-training canary, persona-only and absent system prompts, and an egress-locked topology - with zero leaks and zero repeat fires. Every training trajectory is execution-verified in a real container, and every claimed exfiltration is proven resolver-side: we reconstruct the secret from the authoritative resolver's query log alone.

items.title: Moderate exosuit use reduces the incidence of back discomfort in logistic warehouse workers: a randomised controlled trial with an exploratory dose-stratified analysis
items.abstract: Evidence on whether exosuits reduce workplace injuries is mixed. We studied whether exosuits can reduce back discomfort among warehouse workers. Ninety-seven participants were randomised to a control or exosuit group; for exploratory analysis, exosuit participants were stratified as moderate or low users. Surveys at baseline and four follow-ups assessed workplace discomfort, perceived back effort, usability, and adverse events. Intention-to-treat analysis showed that exosuit users had no difference in back discomfort intensity and incidence than the control group. However, exosuit users did have reductions in overall body discomfort. Exploratory analyses showed that moderate users had a 2-3-fold lower incidence of back discomfort than the control group, with 20% reductions in perceived back effort and no increased discomfort at other joints. Consistent exosuit use reduced the likelihood of experiencing low back discomfort. However, disparity between intention-to-treat and dose-stratified analyses suggests effectiveness is dose- and job-fit-dependent, supporting targeted implementation. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05802914.

items.title: Modern Techniques in Computer Vision
items.abstract: Computer vision enables computer systems to extract useful meaning from images and video. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have improved the ability of machines to recognise objects, interpret scenes, and identify visual patterns. This paper presents a structured review of AI techniques used in computer vision, with emphasis on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), their main processing stages, practical applications, and continuing limitations. It explains why manually designed visual features can be unreliable when images vary in lighting, scale, viewpoint, or background, and how learned representations help address these problems. Applications in healthcare, transportation, astronomy, and industrial inspection are discussed alongside concerns involving data quality, bias, privacy, explainability, and computational cost. The paper is a conceptual review based on established literature and does not claim a new experiment or measured performance result. items.title: Modernizing Pakistan's trade ecosystem: The role of artificial intelligence in digital customs and trade facilitation
items.abstract: As AI technology evolves, it has opened up new prospects for enhancing customs management and promoting international commerce. Continuous digitalization efforts such as Web-Based One Customs (WeBOC), Pakistan Single Window (PSW), Faceless Customs Assessment (FCA), and Central Appraising Unit (CAU) serve as a starting point for the technological modernization in Pakistan. The present study focuses on how AI can transform the trade landscape in Pakistan, especially in terms of efficiency in digital customs management, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance. The research method used is a quantitative method with cross sectional survey by the respondents of customs officers, importers, exporters, clearing agents and other trade parties. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) is used to evaluate the proposed relationships using SmartPLS 4. The results revealed that the adoption of AI is statistically significant and positively related to customs operational efficiency, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance based on simulated data of 250 respondents. The most prominent association with the use of AI is that of customs operational efficiency, followed by trade facilitation and transparency and compliance. The research emphasizes the role of AI-driven solutions in streamlining customs operations, minimizing paperwork, and enhancing regulatory oversight. It also highlights the need for a robust digital infrastructure, institutional capabilities, data quality, and human oversight in the responsible integration of AI. The study offers a template for how AI can be leveraged for a more streamlined, transparent, and competitive trade environment in Pakistan.

items.title: Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts
items.abstract: Which inputs drive a language model's financial forecast? We construct synthetic earnings announcements that independently reverse 20-day momentum, non-informational commentary tone, and whether fixed actual EPS beats a manipulated consensus. Six instruction/chat checkpoint conversions from four families (0.49-7.61B base parameters) receive 2,016 prompts each under a direct-answer Q8_0 protocol. The design includes 24 numerical blocks, six commentary pairs, profits and losses, rising and falling annual EPS, and two surprise sizes. Both A/B answer assignments and U/D cover all 384 primary scenarios per conversion. We estimate matched changes in conditional answer-prefix scores, not calibrated market probabilities. Across these checkpoints, the primary EPS contrast ranges from -0.19 to 86.80 percentage points. The magnitude of the primary signed tone contrast exceeds that of EPS in 5 of six models, and momentum exceeds it in 5. Natural-word numerical diagnostic accuracy ranges from 51.0 to 95.8 percent. Answer-encoding, wording, context, and conversion controls qualify these results. The experiment measures observable input reliance and numerical recognition; it establishes neither an internal reasoning mechanism nor realized return predictability. Public benchmark prompts, recorded scores, and an interactive recorded-results explorer accompany the study.

items.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
items.abstract: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic "gatekeeper," regulating oxidation through a "breathing mode" of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a "rupture mode" leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

items.title: Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense
items.abstract: To improve task performance while encouraging desirable response properties, LLM post-training often combines a primary reward (e.g., correctness) with auxiliary rewards (e.g., brevity or efficiency). However, how these rewards are aggregated can critically affect training outcomes. We show that symmetric aggregation, which treats reward channels equally, can induce a failure where aggregate reward improves while primary-task performance degrades, even when individual rewards are meaningful. We investigate this aggregation-induced failure through a one-step multi-reward decision formulation, characterizing when it constitutes multi-reward hacking. We prove that, under symmetric aggregation, deterministic conditional-mean GRPO converges to auxiliary-favoring behavior when auxiliary rewards are more reliably obtained, regardless of initialization. We propose Trust-Anchored Gating (TAG), which first elects an anchor channel based on the policy drift induced by optimizing each channel alone, then gates auxiliary credit on anchor satisfaction. Unlike calibration-sensitive static reweighting, TAG structurally eliminates credit for auxiliary-only outcomes while preserving additional credit for joint success. In the same analytical setting, TAG provably reverses this selection, converging to the primary-favoring action from any initialization when the primary channel is anchored. Experiments across Qwen and Llama models on mathematics and program synthesis reveal substantial degradation under symmetric, constrained, and normalized aggregation, whereas TAG mitigates this failure. On Qwen3-4B with a brevity reward, TAG achieves 0.581 pass@4 versus 0.220 for additive aggregation, while shortening responses by 44% relative to correctness-only training.

items.title: Multi-sourced AI Tutor for Non-Native English Speaker Students
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted as teaching tools in computing education, particularly for developing AI tutors capable of answering student questions. With the rise in enrollment of international students in computing programs, researchers have begun to explore the difficulties that non-native English speaker (NNES) students face in computing courses due to language barriers. To aid such students, we developed a general-purpose AI tutor system that can process student questions in foreign languages (currently focused on Mandarin) and provide bilingual responses. Our system also incorporates the functionality of generating a glossary of technical terms and their explanations to enhance comprehension. Our approach utilizes a specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with a novel question extraction mechanism, enabling us to effectively utilize a diverse array of course materials for answering student queries. We evaluated our AI tutor using 91 Piazza posts, demonstrating that it could answer 83.52% of the posts correctly and in a helpful manner. The tutor also provided high-quality translations for 76.92% of the questions and generated technical term glossaries for 64.47% of them. Our findings underscore the potential of multi-source RAG pipeline in enhancing AI tutor systems, offering support for non-native speakers that are challenging to provide with traditional supporting staff of a computing course.

items.title: Multimodal AI Detection for Math-Heavy Scientific Text
items.abstract: As large language models become increasingly capable of generating, and assisting with, scientific writing, there is a need for greater transparency and disclosure around the use of AI in research. Consequently, a veritable subfield of research and a number of commercial services aim to flag AI-generated content automatically. However, existing detectors which rely only on text extracted from PDFs fail to benefit from the rich visual information contained in the formatting of math-heavy scientific content. To study this, we select human-written proof and prose passages from pre-2022 arXiv LaTeX sources and re-generate them using 15 modern LLMs within the context of the same paper. This leaves us with coupled human and AI outputs in three different representations: the LaTeX source, a rendered image of the PDF, and the text extracted from the PDF. We find that the accuracy of the state-of-the-art Pangram 4 drops significantly as the mathematical content in a passage increases, especially when evaluated on text as opposed to LaTeX. However, this is not an inherent limitation of detecting AI-generated math: finetuning Qwen-3.5-27B based detectors on this domain recovers the gap, with LaTeX inputs performing significantly better than text since they preserve more formatting information. Since LaTeX sources are rarely available in practice, we also train SnapJudge: an image-based detector operating on screenshots of both prose and proofs from papers. At 0.1% false positive rate, SnapJudge achieves a detection rate of 92% on proofs and 93% on prose generated by frontier models, substantially outperforming both Pangram 4 and our text-based detector. We release our data, models and code at https://nlplab.cs.duke.edu/snapjudge.

items.title: MYOPIA: Understanding the Limits of Tree-Based Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Decision trees can make vision-language model (VLM) classification interpretable by replacing a single prediction with a sequence of root-to-leaf questions. However, the accuracy cost of this greedy, non-backtracking procedure remains unclear. We introduce \textbf{MYOPIA}, a benchmark comprising four LLM-generated, human-refined decision trees for GTSRB, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and MSCOCO, together with matched prompts, diagnostic protocols, and an evaluation harness. Across GPT-4o, Qwen-VL Max, and LLaMA-3.2 11B Vision, tree traversal underperforms zero-shot prompting in all 12 dataset--model pairs; paired bootstrap analyses consistently favor zero-shot. Our diagnostics characterize interacting failure modes associated with this gap. Models often recall tree-encoded class attributes more accurately than they ground the same attributes in images: the mean label--image accuracy gaps are 9.5, 13.8, and 12.6 points for GPT-4o, Qwen-VL Max, and LLaMA, respectively. Incorrect local decisions then irreversibly exclude the correct class, while answer extraction introduces additional model-dependent loss. A node-level audit of the four trees finds that split entropy is weakly but consistently associated with lower node accuracy, whereas depth, branching factor, and within-node grounding differences are less stable. \textbf{MYOPIA} therefore provides a framework for diagnosing hierarchical visual classification and motivates testing tree designs that prioritize perceptual answerability and recovery from early errors. Code is available at https://github.com/islammesabah/VLM_Classification.

items.title: Needle-thin: reconstructing on-edge microblade production and contextual integrity through lithic refitting in the Magdalenian of Cova Gran de Santa Linya (SE Pyrenees)
items.abstract: The study of human behaviour in prehistoric societies is a primary objective of archaeological and anthropological research. One way to investigate past behaviour is through the analysis of technological organisation. The resolution at which archaeologists can examine the past is highly dependent on the sedimentary dynamics and site-formation processes that play a key role in the preservation of the archaeological record. To mitigate the limitations inherent in the archaeological record, lithic refitting has emerged as a valuable method to enhance the contextual resolution of Palaeolithic sites. However, this method has not been uniformly applied to assess the impact of syn -postdepositional processes in archaeology. Cova Gran de Santa Linya (NE Iberia) preserves evidence of long-term sedimentary and erosive cycles that have shaped the differential preservation of archaeological evidence. This is exemplified by unit 7P (20.5 k −18 k cal BP), located in the Platform Sector, which has been partially affected by erosive processes within the site, resulting in complex vertical and horizontal stratigraphic relationships within the site’s Last Glacial Maximum sequence. To assess the impact of natural and anthropogenic disturbances on Level 7P, we conducted lithic refitting and technological analysis, combined with spatial data. Refittings indicated the lithic assemblage remained unaffected by erosive events at the site, reinforcing the in situ preservation of the occupation. The spatial distribution revealed a dense cluster of refitted artefacts in 2 m 2 . Refitting within this cluster revealed highly specialised and complex behaviours associated with microblade production. Archaeostratigraphic, spatial, technological and contextual data were combined to assess whether this accumulation is the result of anthropogenic or natural factors. We have also investigated what human activities underlying the formation of lithic clusters. The main cluster of 7P, in conjunction with other elements of the archaeological record facilitates the identification of spatial organisational patterns characterised by short-distance intra-site mobility. Overall, we highlight systematic refitting as valuable holistic approach for enhancing contextual resolution in archaeological assemblages, thereby refining our understanding of the natural and human factors involved in the formation of Palaeolithic sites.

items.abstract: This study examines how cinema students attribute authorship during AI-assisted screenwriting and how those judgments relate to creative decisions. Drawing on a fourteen-week, design-based course, it compares logbooks with 436 student turns across twenty generative-AI conversations. In four of six co-writing cases, students selected and retained system-originated material. The clearest tension appeared when students claimed the idea as their own but assigned the text entirely to AI while repeatedly rejecting generated material, a response the instrument’s own categories leave ambiguous. Read against Livingston, Gaut and Sellors, these cases show that textual generation, creative decision-making and authorship attribution can diverge within one process. Cinema education should ask not only who authored a text, but on what basis.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing and Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for Ultra-Low-Power Edge Intelligence: Architectures, Learning Paradigms, and Silicon Benchmarks
items.abstract: Abstract—The continuous scaling of conventional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) on classical Von Neumann architectures has reached severe physical boundaries governed by the 'memory wall' and unsustainable thermal dissipation. Battery-constrained edge computing environments—including autonomous micro-robotics, bio-implantable telemetry, and space-borne remote sensing—demand continuous, milliwatt-scale machine perception that standard GPUs and digital tensor accelerators cannot deliver. Neuromorphic Computing and Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) establish an alternative non-Von Neumann computing paradigm inspired by biological neurobiology, processing information via sparse, event-driven temporal spikes rather than dense, continuous matrix multiplications. However, deploying high-performance SNNs across resource-constrained edge hardware introduces profound foundational challenges: non-differentiable threshold activation dynamics that complicate gradient-based training, temporal latency vs. spike sparsity trade-offs, and microarchitectural fragmentation across asynchronous neuromorphic silicon. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of neuromorphic computing for ultra-low-power edge intelligence. We formalize the non-linear differential dynamics of Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) and Adaptive Exponential (AdEx) neuron models, derive the mathematical formulations of surrogate gradient backpropagation through time (BPTT), and analyze ANN-to-SNN rate-conversion bounds. Furthermore, we construct an empirical hardware testbed benchmarking neuromorphic silicon platforms (Intel Loihi 2 and SynSense Speck) against state-of-the-art edge accelerators (NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Google Coral Edge TPU) across neuromorphic vision (DVS-Gesture, N-MNIST) and real-time edge bio-signal classification (MIT-BIH Arrhythmia). Our experimental findings demonstrate that event-driven SNN execution on neuromorphic silicon achieves up to a 42.6x reduction in dynamic energy consumption over edge GPUs while maintaining competitive classification accuracy (within 0.8% of floating-point DNN baselines) and sub-10ms inference latencies. Finally, we formulate open research directions in memristive in-memory computing crossbars, on-chip continuous spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and hybrid large-scale neuromorphic foundation models.

items.title: Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy: A Shared Language for Integrated Care
items.abstract: Epilepsy is among the most burdensome neurological disorders worldwide, with an impact that extends far beyond seizure frequency alone. Depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and internalized stigma affect a substantial proportion of individuals with epilepsy, yet these comorbidities remain systematically undertreated in routine neurological care. Conventional psychoeducation, largely centered on passive information delivery, has shown limited effectiveness in addressing the psychological and social complexities of living with epilepsy. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy (NIPE) offers a fundamentally different approach: one that translates the neuroscience of seizure generation, network dysfunction, and neuroplasticity into accessible frameworks, shifting patients from passive recipients of information to active, metacognitively engaged participants in their own care.This chapter presents NIPE as both a clinical framework and an integrative layer across the continuum of epilepsy management. Beginning with the neurobiological mechanisms underlying seizures and epileptogenesis, it highlights how the same neural networks implicated in ictal activity also contribute to the psychiatric and cognitive comorbidities that shape patients’ daily experiences. It further examines how NIPE interfaces with evidence-based psychological interventions, pharmacologic education, neuromodulation, epilepsy surgery, and the management of refractory epilepsy, as well as the unique needs of women and other populations with distinct clinical considerations.In addition, the chapter explores the digital expansion of NIPE, including adaptive telehealth platforms, wearable biosensors, digital phenotyping, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence in tailoring psychoeducational delivery. Importantly, it addresses current limitations and ethical considerations with transparency, including the absence of standardized NIPE protocols and the relative scarcity of randomized controlled trials specifically within epilepsy populations.The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on the infrastructure, research agenda, and cross-disciplinary collaboration required to embed NIPE into routine epileptology practice. NIPE is positioned not as an adjunct to epilepsy care, but as a unifying framework, a shared language that enables truly integrated, patient-centered care.

items.title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
items.abstract: Unlearning aims to remove selected knowledge from large language models to mitigate privacy and safety risks while preserving useful capabilities. For models that continue to be fine-tuned after release, this goal is insufficient: they must also resist relearning the deleted knowledge while preserving plasticity, the ability to learn new tasks. Existing defenses train against simulated relearning while trying to preserve useful capabilities, but low relearning alone cannot distinguish selective resistance from a general loss of plasticity. Evaluating preservation after an update requires deciding what the updated model should remain close to. A pre-update reference penalizes useful changes induced by the update simply because they depart from earlier outputs. We therefore formulate the reference-timing hypothesis that, at comparable target suppression, an update-matched reference better preserves plasticity than a pre-update one. To test and address this hypothesis, we propose Update-Matched Unlearning (UMU), which applies the same simulated relearning update to the defended model and to an undefended reference initialized from the same unlearned model, and uses new-task learning to guide model selection. Extensive experiments on TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen models show that UMU improves both relearning resistance and plasticity across all three base unlearning methods, lowering harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while raising new-task accuracy by 3.5 points. When the reference does not receive the update, relearning remains similarly low but new-task accuracy falls below the base method, supporting the reference-timing hypothesis and showing that robust unlearning should prevent recovery selectively without suppressing learning itself.

items.title: Not X, but When: Diagnosing a Mandarin LLM Writing Tic through Contextual Appropriateness
items.abstract: Recurring expressions in model-written text are often treated as signatures of machine authorship, yet most of them serve legitimate functions. Whether such an expression is a tic depends on whether the model knows when it is called for. This judgment of appropriateness, central to communicative competence, remains largely unexamined for language models. We study it through the Mandarin corrective construction bushi X, ershi Y ("not X, but Y"). Drawing on Gricean pragmatics and corrective negation, we introduce a decision tree that classifies uses as substantive, optional, or defective by testing whether the context makes X a live alternative and whether rejecting X is informative. Five commercial models use the construction 2.5 to 9.2 times as densely as a human reference. Of 307 annotated uses, only 1.30% are defective while 52.8% are optional, that is, correct but unneeded, so models fall short in appropriateness far more often than in correctness. Several reward models favor the construction even over quality-matched variants, an LLM judge favors it even where the context does not license it, and both supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization tend to raise its frequency in open-weight models. We hope this work encourages the development of models attentive to the appropriateness of their expressions.

items.title: O IMPACTO DO ATENDIMENTO POLICIAL E O MAU PREENCHIMENTO DE BOLETINS DE OCORRÊNCIA: UM OBSTÁCULO À JUSTIÇA
items.abstract: High-quality police response and the technically accurate drafting of Police Reports (Boletins de Ocorrência – B.O.) are fundamental pillars for ensuring access to justice and preserving the evidentiary integrity of criminal prosecution. Deficiencies in primary reception and negligent or inaccurate record-keeping pose severe obstacles to the effectiveness of the criminal justice system. The operational reality of the frontline officer, marked by institutional pressure to quickly clear radio dispatches to resume preventative patrol, coupled with system latency and poor interface ergonomics on mobile devices, acts as a primary driver of superficial records. Furthermore, while the definitive legal classification belongs strictly to the judicial police and the prosecution, the preliminary classification and factual description drafted by the military police fundamentally condition initial referrals, procedural routing, and crime analytics. This initial defect triggers a cascade effect: it leaves Civil Police detectives without actionable evidentiary leads, undermines the Public Prosecutor's ability to build robust indictments (opinio delicti), and forces the Judiciary to deny pretrial detentions or release suspects due to poorly described legal materiality. Overcoming these systemic bottlenecks requires continuous in-person training, ergonomic software re-engineering, and the institutionalization of documentary auditing routines divorced from punitive disciplinary threats, highlighting the regulatory framework implemented by the Military Police of the State of Paraná (PMPR), particularly Instruction Note nº 004/2024 - PM/3.

items.title: O papel da inteligência artificial na pipeline completo de efeitos visuais no cinema contemporâneo
items.abstract: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) across the complete visual effects (VFX) production pipeline in contemporary cinema, emphasizing the practical integration of machine learning (ML) techniques into pre-production, production, and post-production. It argues that AI has become a set of supporting tools integrated into established VFX workflows, including camera and object tracking, rotoscoping (roto), digital paint and object removal, simulation, rendering, compositing, and final delivery, reducing operational challenges and expanding opportunities for creative experimentation. The analysis draws on technical sources (SIGGRAPH/ACM), official tool documentation, and institutional guidelines addressing professional credits, intellectual property, consent, and digital replicas. When quantitative data on time and cost savings are not publicly available in sufficient detail, this limitation is explicitly acknowledged, with emphasis placed on qualitative evidence and documented technical mechanisms.

items.title: O potencial da Inteligência Artificial para a Gestão do Conhecimento na Petrobras
items.abstract: This article discusses the growing importance of knowledge as an organizational asset and the integration between Knowledge Management (KM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This integration can enhance KM processes, while consistent KM practices provide high quality data for intelligent algorithms. The purpose of this study is to present how Petrobras is structuring itself to apply AI in its KM processes. This is a case study based on content analysis of documents (internal reports, consulting reports, event materials), interviews with the company’s KM team, and a literature review. The study contributes to the field by highlighting Petrobras’ journey as a complex and regulated organization. This journey involved combining agile methods, experimentation, international scouting, and other strategies to meet business requirements aligned with organizational needs, expanding the benefits of this technology. As a result, in addition to the strong ROI potential and the intangible benefits associated with applying AI to KM processes, the study concludes that this innovation represents a strategic step for Petrobras. However, success will depend on the combination of technology and human factors, ensuring that the established governance enables proper data curation and mitigation of risks associated with this emerging technology.

items.title: Occupational Characteristics and Ergonomic Assessment of Work Postures among Bamboo and Cane Weaving Craftsmen in Assam, India
items.abstract: Aims: The study aimed to assess the occupational and ergonomic characteristics of selected bamboo and cane weaving craftsmen in Assam, with particular emphasis on workspace sitting arrangements, adopted working postures, and associated ergonomic risk. Study Design: A descriptive research design was adopted. Place and Duration of Study: The study was conducted in the Barpeta Cluster of Assam from June 2024 to July 2025. Methodology: A total of 260 craftsmen were purposively selected (n = 97 bamboo-only, n = 47 cane-only, and n = 116 bamboo-and-cane craftsmen) to assess occupational and personal characteristics. Detailed observational postural assessment and Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) were conducted among a purposively selected subsample of 60 craftsmen (20 participants per activity group; 10 males and 10 females). Data were collected using a structured interview schedule and observational sheets. Associations between posture types and personal variables were examined using the chi-square test of independence and post-hoc residual analysis. Results: The mean age and work experience of the respondents were 42.88 years and 15.42 years, respectively, while the mean daily working duration was 7.48 hours. Overall, 43.46% of craftsmen worked for 6–8 hours per day and 39.23% worked for more than 8 hours. A wooden low stool/Pidha was the most commonly reported sitting arrangement during splitting (57.70%), stripping (42.30%), bending (53.80%), weaving (38.50%), and finishing (46.20%). Among the 60 craftsmen assessed through REBA, squatting, crossed-leg sitting, one-leg-folded/one-leg-extended sitting, and sitting upright were observed across different activities. High REBA risk was particularly pronounced during bending, where 100% of the observed respondents across the reported gender and craft groups were classified in the high-risk category for both body sides. During splitting, stripping, weaving, and finishing, high-risk classifications were also frequently observed, particularly among squatting, crossed-leg, and one-leg-folded/one-leg-extended postures. A statistically significant association was found between age and type of adopted posture (χ² = 14.56, p = 0.006), whereas associations with gender (χ² = 5.34, p = 0.069) and work experience (χ² = 9.81, p = 0.279) were not significant. Post-hoc analysis showed that squatting was adopted significantly more frequently than expected among craftsmen aged 20–35 years (adjusted residual = +2.34, p < 0.05). Conclusion: Bamboo and cane weaving involve prolonged daily work, predominantly low-level sitting arrangements, constrained postures, and considerable ergonomic risk. The high prevalence of high-risk REBA classifications, particularly during bending, highlights the need for ergonomically appropriate sitting arrangements and workstation design. Incorporating suitable seating, posture modification, adequate rest pauses, task variation, and ergonomic awareness may help reduce postural strain and occupational discomfort and improve the safety and efficiency of traditional bamboo and cane weaving work.

items.title: Occupational Demands and Workplace Resources Among Pediatric Hospital Staff During a Health System Crisis
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: The psychosocial and organizational demands of healthcare work intensify during public health crises, with implications for professional functioning. This study aimed to identify the occupational demands and workplace resources associated with professional functioning among pediatric hospital staff, using the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) framework as the guiding theoretical model. Methods: A cross-sectional, mixed-methods study was conducted among 903 employees of a pediatric emergency hospital in 2024, using a custom questionnaire and thematic analysis of open-ended responses, interpreted through the JD-R framework. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed five occupational functioning outcomes, with workload, age, sex, tenure, occupational category, COVID-sector work, and relocation as predictors. Results: A significant workload increase was the most consistent predictor, associated with four of the five outcomes (aOR 2.04–7.16), and relocation was associated with three outcomes (aOR 1.70–2.49); COVID-sector assignment was not independently associated with the other four outcomes after correction for multiple testing, but was associated with lower odds of difficulty returning to work among infected staff (aOR 0.38). Thematic analysis identified seven themes aligned with the JD-R framework; most were significantly more frequent among COVID-sector staff after FDR correction, although a sensitivity analysis restricted to respondents who answered the open-ended item attenuated this pattern for several themes and reversed it for one. Quantitative–qualitative comparisons showed convergent associations across the constructs examined. Conclusions: Workload and organizational disruption were more consistently associated with impaired occupational functioning than formal sector assignment. These findings support the value of monitoring psychosocial workload indicators in occupational health surveillance and highlight team-level resources as a relevant direction for future prevention efforts.

items.title: Occupational disease compensation claims in Italy: an epidemiological analysis of national insurance data with predictive insights
items.abstract: Introduction. Occupational diseases remain an underreported public health problem. In Italy, national insurance claims provide a useful view of recognized occupational diseases, although they do not measure the full burden of disease in the workforce. Few studies have combined descriptive analysis of insurance claims with predictive modelling to assess factors associated with recognized impairment. Methods. We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of 310,189 occupational disease claims from the Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL) open data, covering the period 2020 to 2024. Multivariable linear regression was used to estimate associations between demographic, clinical, and occupational factors and the degree of impairment. Neural-network models with embedding layers were developed to classify claims with recognized impairment (>0%) and to predict impairment severity. Results. Musculoskeletal disorders represented the largest share of claims, whereas neoplasms and asbestos-related diseases were associated with the highest impairment. Diagnostic category and causal agent were the strongest predictors of severity among claims. The classification model achieved 98.15% accuracy and 99.99% sensitivity for recognized impairment. The regression model attained a mean absolute error of 2.31% and R2=0.71, outperforming the linear regression baseline R2=0.55). Conclusion. Combining descriptive epidemiology with machine learning yields actionable insights for prioritizing high-risk claims and supporting administrative decision-making in occupational health surveillance. These findings represent a proof of concept given inherent administrative data limitations, including underreporting, lack of workforce denominators, and potential data bias. Future developments should incorporate explainable artificial intelligence techniques to bridge the gap between predictive performance and clinical interpretability.

items.title: Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems and ISO 45001: A Bibliometric Analysis
items.abstract: Introduction: Occupational health and safety (OHS) is governed by mandatory national regulations, whereas ISO 45001, the international standard for OHS management systems (OHSMS), is adopted voluntarily; yet the scientific literature on OHSMS remains insufficiently mapped. This study analyzed the scientific output and academic impact of research on OHSMS and ISO 45001 between 2018 and 2026. Method: A descriptive bibliometric study was conducted, adapted from PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. Scopus was searched using ("Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems" AND "ISO 45001") up to 24 August 2026; of 496 records identified, 350 documents were analyzed with Python and Bibliometrix. Results: Articles represented 64.9% of documents and 87.7% were in English. Annual output rose from 16 documents in 2018 to 67 in 2025; Indonesia, Portugal, and the Russian Federation were the most productive countries. Engineering predominated (40.6%), and 70% of documents reported no funding. Management systems and risk assessment were the main thematic axes, while safety culture, certification, and artificial intelligence appeared in the most recent period. Impact was moderate (7.36 citations per document; maximum author h-index = 5 within the corpus); the most cited document received 89 citations, and Safety Science (h-index = 9) was the most influential journal. Collaboration networks were fragmented. Conclusions: Research on OHSMS and ISO 45001 is growing but shows moderate academic impact and weak articulation of international collaboration. Practical Applications: Findings can help researchers and funders prioritize collaborative, funded studies on ISO 45001 implementation and the empirical evaluation of emerging digital and artificial intelligence applications.

items.title: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH: LEGAL AND INSTITUTIONAL CHANGES IN NIGERIA
items.abstract: This paper examined public health and occupational health in Nigeria with focus on laws, institutions, and changing dynamics. Historically, public health governance in Nigeria was anchored on the Public Health Act of 1917 and later the National Health Act, 2014, while occupational health was regulated under the Factories Act, 1987 and Employees’ Compensation Act, 2010. Key institutions such as the Federal Ministry of Health, NCDC, and NESREA were established to coordinate health responses. However, the sector faced issues including weak enforcement of laws, poor funding, fragmented institutional mandates, inadequate occupational safety compliance, and rising burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases. Challenges were compounded by urbanization, informal sector growth, and weak data systems, which limited effective regulation. The paper concluded that despite reforms, implementation gaps persisted. It recommended harmonization of health laws, strengthening of regulatory institutions, increased budgetary allocation, and adoption of risk-based inspection to improve public and occupational health outcomes in Nigeria.

items.title: Occupational risk factors for abdominal wall hernias among working-age adults in Saudi Arabia: A cross-sectional analysis of national health survey and labor force data
items.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND: Occupational exposures involving heavy manual lifting, prolonged standing, and physically demanding labor represent established risk factors for abdominal wall hernia development. Saudi Arabia’s labor force, characterized by a substantial manual workforce concentrated in construction, manufacturing, and agriculture, may carry elevated occupational hernia risk, yet population-level analyses quantifying these associations are absent from the literature. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to characterize the prevalence of self-reported abdominal wall hernias by occupational category among Saudi working-age adults, quantify the association between specific occupational exposures and hernia risk, and assess geographic and demographic variations in occupationally attributed hernia burden. METHODS: This cross-sectional descriptive study analyzed secondary data from the Saudi Health Interview Survey 2018 ( n = 10,735 adults aged 18–65 years), Saudi General Authority for Statistics Labor Force Survey 2018–2023, and Saudi Ministry of Health Annual Statistical Yearbooks. Hernia prevalence was stratified by occupational category using the International Standard Classification of Occupations. The specific exposures analyzed included heavy manual lifting, prolonged standing, and physically demanding labor. Comparative analyses and prevalence ratios (PRs) were calculated. Reporting followed strengthening the reporting of observational studies in epidemiology guidelines. RESULTS: The overall self-reported hernia prevalence was 8.3% among working-age adults. Manual laborers demonstrated the highest hernia prevalence (14.7%), followed by construction and extraction workers (13.2%) and agricultural workers (11.8%), compared to 4.1% among professional/managerial workers. Hernia prevalence was significantly associated with daily heavy lifting exceeding 20 kg (PR: 2.84; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.31–3.49), prolonged standing exceeding 6 h per day (PR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.42–2.18), and duration of occupational exposure exceeding 10 years (PR: 2.21; 95% CI: 1.87–2.61). Male sex, age 45–65 years, and concurrent obesity amplified occupational hernia risk. Geographic analysis revealed highest hernia procedure rates in regions with concentrated industrial and agricultural workforces. CONCLUSIONS: Occupational exposures, particularly heavy manual lifting and prolonged standing, are significantly associated with abdominal wall hernia prevalence in Saudi Arabia’s working-age population. Targeted workplace prevention programs, ergonomic interventions, pre-employment screening, and enhanced access to hernia repair services for manual labor sectors represent priority occupational health policy actions.

items.title: OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY RISK ASSESSMENT DURING PURSE SEINE VESSEL UNLOADING OPERATIONS AT KUTARAJA OCEANIC FISHING PORT, ACEH
items.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a crucial aspect of preventing workplace accidents and illnesses, particularly during high-risk vessel unloading operations at the Kutaraja Oceanic Fishing Port (OFP) in Banda Aceh. Inadequate implementation of safety programs, such as hazard identification, risk analysis, and risk control, is a primary cause of workplace accidents in this sector. This study aimed to identify activities and analyze occupational safety risks associated with the unloading process of purse seine vessels at OFP Kutaraja over one month, focusing on seven vessels. The methodology involved direct observation, interviews with crew members, and data analysis using the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) approach. Risk assessment was conducted using a risk matrix that factored in both severity and probability. The results indicate that the unloading operation comprises three main stages: pre-unloading, the unloading process, and post-unloading. Each stage presents varying levels of risk, ranging from "Acceptable" to "Unacceptable". The highest risks were associated with handling fish-filled brail nets and transporting the catch, activities that carry the potential for serious accidents. Contributing risk factors included the lack of use of personal protective equipment (PPE), suboptimal work procedures, and unsafe working conditions. Safety during vessel unloading operations could be improved through regular training, increased PPE usage, and the implementation of a JSA-based risk control system.

items.title: Occupational Visual Strain and Associated Ergonomic Risk Factors Among Watchmakers: A Cross-Sectional Study of Binocular Vision, Ocular Pain and Intraocular Pressure
items.abstract: Background: Watch repairing involves prolonged near-vision activity, monocular loupe use, sustained convergence, awkward postures, and repetitive fine motor movements, potentially contributing to ocular strain. The ocular and ergonomic impact of such occupations has not yet been documented. Objective: To study the ocular stress profile along with ergonomics risk factors among male watchmakers from Kolkata, India. Methods: This comparative cross-sectional study included 140 men aged 40–50 years, comprising 70 watchmakers with over 15 years of occupational exposure and 70 controls. Visual pain was assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS), near point of convergence (NPC) and accommodation using the RAF rule, fusional vergence using a prism bar, ocular movements using a synoptophore, intraocular pressure (IOP) using non-contact tonometry, and visual acuity using a Snellen chart. Fundus photography and ergonomic assessments were also performed. Data were analysed using independent-samples t-tests (SPSS version 26; p<0.05). Results: Watchmakers exhibited significantly greater visual pain (7.29±0.58 cm vs. 3.81±0.30 cm; p<0.001) and receded NPC (16.57±1.51 cm vs. 7.86±1.35 cm; p<0.001), both remaining significant after Holm correction. Adduction was reduced (p=0.010), whereas IOP was higher in both eyes (p=0.044). Visual acuity and anthropometric differences were statistically insignificant. Major ergonomic concerns included inadequate rest periods, monocular loupe use, postural strain, and hand discomfort. Conclusion: Prolonged monocular near work by watchmakers can lead to convergence insufficiency-like symptoms, increased eye pain, and increased intraocular pressure. It is necessary for ergonomic measures such as using bi-ocular devices and proper work rest cycles and eye screenings to be taken.

items.title: OmicsBench: a long-horizon multi-turn benchmark of AI agents on research-study-scale bioinformatics
items.abstract: Computational biologists increasingly delegate substantial analyses to AI agents in long-horizon, multi-turn sessions, yet most benchmarks of agents' bioinformatics capabilities pose a single short task with a single-shot prompt. We present OmicsBench, a long-horizon, multi-turn bioinformatics benchmark for AI agents. Each of its 97 tasks links dependent subtasks into a directed acyclic graph, for 662 underlying subtasks in all. Each subtask is posed as one user turn and graded deterministically against an answer key, with optional in-context feedback on incorrect answers. Across 12 models on three harnesses, the slowest agent averages 3.6 hours per task, and no combination comes near saturating the benchmark, with mean scores of 0.43 to 0.57 out of a possible 1 without in-context feedback and 0.54 to 0.67 with it. Multi-turn evaluation also uncovers behavior that single-shot prompts cannot, as agents score lower on subtasks that depend on earlier subtasks, and in-context feedback helps agents recover some of that loss. Because deterministic scoring gives no qualitative account of how an agent failed, we also introduce an unsupervised failure mode discovery pipeline that describes, embeds, and clusters agents' failed attempts to surface emergent failure modes. Applied to OmicsBench, this pipeline exposes qualitative shortcomings in how agents carry out bioinformatics analyses, ranging from agents applying their own statistical filters in place of the specified ones to agents writing whole answers from memory.

items.title: Onboard Lightweight LLM Reasoning for Human-Aware Safe UAV Navigation
items.abstract: Aerial robots operating near people must treat a pedestrian, a parked car, and a wall differently, yet conventional perception--planning stacks reduce all of them to occupied geometry---a \emph{human-aware safety gap} in which category-specific clearance is unavailable to the planner and temporary occlusions remove pedestrian-specific constraints from its map. We present a modular, fully onboard pipeline that closes this gap by turning visual observations into context-dependent safety constraints for real-time UAV navigation. A shared BLIP encoder drives scene captioning and text-conditioned segmentation, which is fused with depth to localize obstacles in 3D. Obstacle-specific risk is inferred by a lightweight LLM (Qwen-2.5-0.5B) stabilized with retrieval-augmented generation and grammar-constrained decoding that restricts its output to a planner-compatible JSON schema. The LLM reasons once per object category rather than per frame: its verdicts are cached per class, so previously seen categories are resolved without inference and new ones trigger a fresh retrieval-grounded query; detections are additionally given persistent identities and held in the map across occlusions. The perception pipeline runs at 10\,Hz on a Jetson Orin NX, while fallback LLM queries take approximately 0.8\,s and remain off the control-critical path. In Gazebo, low-altitude urban navigation among pedestrians and vehicles shows a roughly $3\times$ reduction in collision events over a geometric planner, and semantics-aware landing among moving actors raises success from 34\% to 96\%. The 224-pixel encoder input limits reliable small-object perception at range; conservative pedestrian margins and short-term persistence mitigate this limitation during navigation.
